name: Light Navy
lede: Light Navy raises the value of [[navy]], tracked since 1927 by the German RAL color standard as RAL 5017, and carries its own lighter child, [[newport]].

sections.title: A standard, not just a survey
sections.body: The name is the modifier *light* set against the base color [[navy]] [1]. Its earliest documented listing in our sources is RAL 5017, from the German RAL color-matching system founded in 1927, an approximate screen value for a paint and signage standard rather than a measured dye [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists separately file the same range as block 183, "dark blue," and the xkcd 2010 survey records it again from crowd labeling [1]. It has one documented child in our data, the still-lighter [[newport]], and its nearest neighbor is [[dusk-blue]] at 2.6 units [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 90 of 23,781 paintings, 0.38 percent, rarer than 53 percent of our named colors; within a single canvas it is a distinct area in 39 of them [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 0.8 percent of that century's 1,674 paintings, 3.9 times the expected rate, and inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 51 percent of its 39 appearances [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1400 panel by the Master of Heiligenkreuz, 527 years before RAL's 1927 record; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2].
